units.function: HTTP workflow for generic approvals, revision/resubmission, comments and mutable links between approvals and issues.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes orchestrate approval, issue-link, comment, Agent and activity services; several responsibility and side-effect rules exist only in this transport layer.
units.keyDataModels: Approval type/status/payload, requester/decider IDs, free-form note, comments and issue-approval links.
units.lifecycle: Agent or board creates an approval, links issues in separate calls, board approves/rejects/requests revision, requester resubmits and participants comment; links remain editable after resolution.
units.testAssessment: Route tests cover actor-derived requester/decider attribution, cross-company protection, payload redaction and idempotent decision responses. They do not require an exact action digest, approval-authority/risk match, immutable target links, evidence/result binding or atomic creation with issue links. Local mode can attribute a decision to the synthetic string 'board'.
units.designRationale: Provide a flexible board inbox that can accommodate several approval types without a schema per type.
units.companyOsProblem: High-risk work must pause on a versioned action contract and resume only after the matching accountable human approves the exact action, permissions, data, evidence expectations and runtime scope.
units.companyOsFit: Actor-derived attribution, hidden cross-tenant existence and idempotent response shape are useful references. Company OS must put approval invariants in application use cases, require a real human principal and make target/action associations immutable after proposal.
units.responsibilityConflict: A mutable issue link and arbitrary payload cannot prove who approved which exact work/action/data contract. Redacting comments before persistence also destroys the original evidence rather than storing a governed original plus derivative.

units.function: Persistence and state transitions for generic approvals, including hire-Agent activation and related post-approval side effects.
units.dependencyDirection: Application service depends directly on Paperclip approval/Agent/company schemas, adapter reconciliation, budget policy and notification hooks.
units.keyDataModels: Generic JSON payload, pending/approved/rejected/revision_requested status, requester/decider/note/timestamps and hire-Agent configuration.
units.lifecycle: Create pending row, compare-and-set a terminal decision, then perform type-specific hire side effects; revision and resubmission are read-then-update transitions.
units.testAssessment: Focused tests cover create/list/get, deduplication, same-decision idempotency and hire-agent behavior. A critical consistency gap remains: approve changes status before hire side effects; if a later side effect fails, retry observes approved and skips those effects permanently. Revision/resubmit updates do not include the prior status in their WHERE clause, so concurrent terminal decisions can be overwritten.
units.designRationale: Keep a small generic approval table while attaching product-specific behavior in one service.
units.companyOsProblem: Approval resolution and effect publication need a crash-safe, replayable saga/outbox with immutable request digest and per-effect receipts.
units.companyOsFit: The compare-and-set terminal transition is a useful primitive, but this implementation must not be reused. Company OS should separate decision receipt from resumable effect execution and preserve every attempt/result under one responsibility record.
units.responsibilityConflict: Status can say approved while the approved organization/runtime change never happened, and the stored record does not bind action, contract, Agent, human, permissions, data, evidence or result digests.

units.function: Many-to-many association service between issues and generic approvals with same-company validation.
units.dependencyDirection: Thin DB service couples Paperclip issue and approval schemas; routes decide who may add or remove links.
units.keyDataModels: Composite issueId/approvalId link plus duplicated companyId.
units.lifecycle: Validate both records share a company, insert idempotently, list either direction or delete the link at any approval status.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover tenant validation, idempotent link creation and deletion. No immutability/status rule prevents post-decision relinking, and no digest or revision records the association used when a human decided.
units.designRationale: Allow one approval to be surfaced from several related work items without embedding arrays in either row.
units.companyOsProblem: Responsibility projection needs immutable, versioned links from an approval receipt to exact work/action/evidence objects.
units.companyOsFit: Same-tenant foreign-key validation is worth retaining conceptually, but Company OS should create append-only responsibility edges inside the proposal transaction and supersede them only through a new contract revision.
units.responsibilityConflict: Post-resolution mutation can change what the audit trail appears to say was approved.

units.function: Canonical-JSON HMAC signing for decision specifications plus secure local generation and persistence of an instance signing secret.
units.dependencyDirection: Server crypto/filesystem adapter is called by the Decision service and depends on Paperclip home-path conventions; no neutral signing port exists.
units.keyDataModels: decision-spec-v1 canonical payload, instance-wide 32-byte-or-longer symmetric secret and version-prefixed SHA-256 HMAC.
units.lifecycle: Resolve explicit secret or atomically publish a generated 0600 key under an owned 0700 directory, sign canonical payload and verify with timing-safe comparison.
units.testAssessment: The implementation defends against partial/concurrent local key creation, ownership and permissive modes. It has no key ID, historical verification set, tenant separation, rotation workflow, asymmetric signer/KMS/HSM adapter or algorithm-agility contract.
units.designRationale: Make tampering detectable in zero-config self-hosting without requiring an external key service.
units.companyOsProblem: Action/approval contracts require deployable-profile-neutral signatures, rotation and durable verification after key changes.
units.companyOsFit: Canonicalization, fail-fast key validation and atomic local creation are strong patterns. Company OS should adapt them behind a SignaturePort with kid/algorithm/tenant/purpose, KMS-capable managed adapter and retained verification keys.
units.responsibilityConflict: A valid instance HMAC proves database content was signed by the instance, not which accountable human consented or whether the signed fields cover the full responsibility contract.

units.function: Agent-originated proposal and bundle API, board decision/dismissal API, Agent cancellation/readback, statistics and a reviewed attention-archive proposal flow.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes validate shared Decision effects and call Decision/attention/authorization services; the API is tied to Paperclip issue and board/Agent actor concepts.
units.keyDataModels: Decision title/body/options/input prompts, typed issue effects, origin Agent/run, expiry/idempotency, continuation policy and signed archive manifest.
units.lifecycle: An in-run Agent proposes bounded effects, board lists and decides, executor applies them and optionally wakes the origin Agent; archive proposals snapshot an exact reviewed manifest.
units.testAssessment: Strict schemas bound option/effect/input counts and agent/board routes constrain proposal versus decision roles. Gaps: every board member can decide regardless of approval authority/risk class; local implicit board is not a real human; most validation errors use English strings rather than mandatory stable codes; generic high-risk data/tool/model actions are not represented.
units.designRationale: Expose a compact human-in-the-loop protocol that an Agent can invoke during one run and continue after a board answer.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector-neutral Agents need pause/resume approval APIs while humans need role/risk-matched decision surfaces independent of a particular work-item model.
units.companyOsFit: Bounded typed effects, origin-run requirement, archive manifest review and continuation are strong API references. Company OS must define its own action envelope, stable error contract, real-human approval authority and Connector protocol instead of copying Paperclip routes/types.
units.responsibilityConflict: Board membership is treated as sufficient approval authority and the API does not require a responsibility-contract/action/data/evidence digest.

units.function: Signed human-decision engine with target snapshots, typed issue effects, origin/decider authorization intersection, per-effect execution ledger, idempotency, expiry, continuation delivery and crash recovery.
units.dependencyDirection: Application service directly owns Paperclip issue, run, authorization, activity and retention schemas/services; effect types are Paperclip work-item mutations rather than a portable execution contract.
units.keyDataModels: Decision/bundle, signed options and target snapshots, chosen option/input values, effect execution receipt, origin Agent/run/issue, deciding user, continuation marker and archive manifest.
units.lifecycle: Validate origin run and authority, snapshot targets transactionally, sign effect specification, CAS open to decided, re-authorize origin and decider, claim and execute each effect transactionally, persist result/audit, recover running work and deliver Agent continuation at least once.
units.testAssessment: A substantial focused suite covers idempotent creation/decision, tamper rejection, exact archive manifests, lost access, stale targets, double decision, per-effect failure/partial success, crash recovery, continuation and bounded sweeps. Important gaps: the signature includes only decision ID, options and target snapshots—not title/body/inputs/expiry/origin responsible human/responsibility contract/data grants/approval authority/input values/evidence policy. The accountable human is re-read from the mutable run during execution. Effects are sequential rather than an atomic business transaction, failed effects are terminal rather than policy-driven retryable, and recovery reconstructs a generic board actor from membership.
units.designRationale: Turn Agent proposals into bounded, tamper-evident, human-selected issue mutations that survive crashes without executing one effect twice.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a canonical high-risk decision/effect engine that can prove exact human responsibility and safely resume Connector work across cloud/local execution nodes.
units.companyOsFit: This is Paperclip's best reference for decision execution and supersedes its generic Approval design. Company OS should adapt signed immutable manifests, authorization intersection, per-effect receipts, staleness policy, CAS and recovery, while owning neutral action/evidence/data contracts and never importing Paperclip schema/types.
units.responsibilityConflict: The signed payload does not freeze the accountable human, approving authority, permissions/data contract, evidence/result obligations or supplied inputs. A later run-row change can alter the origin human shown in audit, so it cannot serve as Company OS's responsibility proof.
